screen1-a1.where: Top row, far left: a small Spanish flag with the number 1 beside it.
screen1-a1.expectation: I think it shows which language course I am on, and pressing it might let me change course. The '1' I cannot place: a level, a score, or a count.
screen1-a1.cue: The flag and the number 1. There is no word.

first_pass.why: I recognise that it is a flag, but I have to work at pictures, and the '1' could mean three different things. I would read it over and over without committing.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Spanish' or 'My courses' under it, and say what the 1 is, for example 'Score 1'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows what it is for and what the number means
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the flag at the top-left once. Look at what opens. Then press the phone's Back button.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make plain what the flag was for, or still leaves the number unexplained
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly shows what the flag is for and what the number counts
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the flag with the 1. A panel dropped down showing my Spanish course, a pale '+ Course' tile, and 'Your Spanish Score is 1' with a bar from 1 to 2. I closed it (pressing the grey area below closed it; see T16). I finished.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: The panel shows that the flag is my course and that the 1 is my Spanish Score. That settles both of my questions.

screen1-a2.where: Top row, second from left: a pale grey flame with a faint number 1.
screen1-a2.expectation: No idea really. Perhaps a count of days of something; a flame does not tell me what.
screen1-a2.cue: A grey flame and the number 1, both very faint.

first_pass.why: A flame is not a word I can hold on to. Nothing tells me what the 1 counts or what pressing it would open, and the grey makes it look switched off.
first_pass.solution: A word beside it, such as '1 day streak', and a clear statement of what opens when I press it.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the flame tells you what it counts
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the flame in the top row. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still does not tell you what the flame and its number mean
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens says plainly what the flame and number are
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the grey flame, which showed 0 on my phone. A page titled 'Streak' opened with a large '0' and 'day streak!', a calendar, and a card about streak freezes. I closed it with the X.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: The page says plainly that the flame is my day streak and the number is how many days. The flame alone still said nothing, so I had to press it to learn, but one press settled it.

screen1-a3.where: Top row, middle: a blue hexagon shape with 520.
screen1-a3.expectation: I guess it is some kind of points or money in the app, and pressing it may take me to a shop.
screen1-a3.cue: The blue shape and the number 520.

first_pass.why: I cannot recognise the blue shape as anything I know. 520 of what? I am guessing that it is money.
first_pass.solution: Label it with a word, for example '520 gems', and make it plain that it opens the shop.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the stone tells you what it is and what it is for
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the blue stone in the top row. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not say what the stones are or what pressing the stone was for
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what the stones are and why you would press it
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the blue stone with 644 (the number differs from the picture). The 'Shop' page opened. It has a card reading 'Watch an ad to earn up to 15 gems', and the same blue stone sits next to 644 at the top. I closed it with the X. I finished.

screen1-a3.closing_comment: It opens the shop, as I guessed, and I can work out from the card that the stones are 'gems'. But nothing says 'you have 644 gems'; I had to put it together myself.

screen1-a4.where: Top row, far right: a pink battery with a lightning bolt and the number 25.
screen1-a4.expectation: I guess it is energy or power left, and pressing it shows how to get more.
screen1-a4.cue: The lightning bolt and the number 25.

first_pass.why: A battery and a bolt suggests energy, but I am not certain it is not charging or power settings. 25 out of what?
first_pass.solution: Write 'Energy 25 of 25' in words.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows it is an app thing (not the phone battery) and what the number is
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the pink bolt-and-battery at the top-right. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still leaves you unsure what it is or what the number means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and what the number means
test_cases.what_happened: On my phone the pink bolt-and-battery showed 25 at the top right. I pressed it and a page titled 'Energy' opened, with a pink bar reading '25 / 25' and ways to get more. I closed it with the X. I finished.

screen1-a4.closing_comment: The page names it 'Energy' and shows 25 out of 25. That is plain, it is the app's energy and not my phone battery, and I would remember it.

screen1-a5.where: The wide green banner under the top row: 'SECTION 1, UNIT 1 — Order at a café'.
screen1-a5.expectation: I think it tells me where I am in the course. If I pressed it, maybe it would show me the unit or let me pick another unit. I am not sure it is a button at all.
screen1-a5.cue: The words 'SECTION 1, UNIT 1' and 'Order at a café'.

first_pass.why: The words tell me where I am, which I value a great deal, but it looks like a heading, not a button. I cannot tell whether pressing it does anything or what.
first_pass.solution: If it is a button, say what it does, for example 'See all units', or give it a visible arrow.

test_cases.targets: whether you can tell it can be pressed, and whether pressing it does what you expected
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the words on the green bar at the top (not the small notebook at its right end). See what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the bar told you it could be pressed, or what opened was not what you expected from the words
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opened is what you expected from the words on the bar
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the words 'Order at a café' on the green bar. After a few seconds a page titled 'Spanish Course' opened, listing Section 1, Section 2 and so on as large cards. I closed it with the X and was back on the path. I finished the task.

screen1-a5.closing_comment: What opened roughly matches what I guessed: a place to see the whole course and choose a part of it. But nothing on the bar itself tells me it can be pressed, and I would not have guessed 'Spanish Course' from 'Section 1, Unit 1'.

screen1-a6.where: Right end of the green banner: a white notebook icon with lines.
screen1-a6.expectation: Probably notes or a guide for this unit, or a list of lessons.
screen1-a6.cue: A picture of a notebook with lines. No words.

first_pass.why: A lined notebook could mean notes, a list, a guidebook, or a menu. I cannot settle on one.
first_pass.solution: The word 'Guide' or 'Notes' beside the icon.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the notebook settles which of your guesses it is
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the small notebook at the right end of the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you guessed, or still does not tell you what the notebook stands for
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches one of your guesses and you would remember it next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the small notebook at the end of the green bar. A page opened with the owl, 'SECTION 1, UNIT 1 — Order at a café', and a list headed 'KEY PHRASES', Spanish sentences with English below. I closed it with the X. I finished.

screen1-a6.closing_comment: It is notes, or a guide for this unit, which was one of my guesses. I am not sure I would remember that the notebook means 'key phrases' next time without a word on it.

screen1-a7.where: Just under the banner on the left: a green owl-like character, a black-and-yellow badge with a skull-like face, and a red exclamation mark.
screen1-a7.expectation: I have no idea. Something wants my attention because of the red exclamation mark, but I cannot tell what.
screen1-a7.cue: The red exclamation mark. The characters mean nothing to me.

first_pass.why: I cannot recognise the character or the badge. There is no word. This is the kind of image I simply cannot read, and I would stop here.
first_pass.solution: Replace it with a plain labelled button, for example 'Event: 13 days left' with a sentence saying what the event is.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the badge tells you what it is and what the red mark was about
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the cartoon owl-and-skull picture at the left, under the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left, or the lower blue text button if there is no X. Do NOT press any button that says it claims on or opens another game.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still does not make plain what this is, or it takes you somewhere you could not have predicted
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and you could predict it next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the owl-and-skull picture. A full page opened: 'Brawl Stars Quest — You got Chaos Drops! Earn more rewards tomorrow', with CLAIM ON BRAWL STARS and CLAIM LATER. There was no X, so I pressed CLAIM LATER. Instead of going back, that opened another page, 'Brawl Stars Quest — INCOMPLETE', showing Day 1 to Day 7 rewards. I closed that with the X and was home. The red mark had gone.

screen1-a7.closing_comment: It is a promotion tied to another game I do not know. 'Claim later' took me somewhere else rather than back, which I could not have predicted. I still would not know what this is next time.

screen1-a8.where: Top of the winding path: on the running app, a round green button with a white star inside a green ring.
screen1-a8.expectation: I think it starts my current lesson, because it is the only coloured one on the path.
screen1-a8.cue: It is green while the others are grey, and it has a ring around it.

first_pass.why: Colour is the only clue. There is no word such as 'Start', so I am inferring that green means 'this one is next'.
first_pass.solution: A label such as 'Start lesson' or 'You are here' on the green button.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the green star shows plainly that it is a lesson
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the round green star button near the top of the path. Read what appears. Do NOT press the button inside what appears; press on an empty part of the path to close it.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not say it is a lesson, or you still could not have known from the star
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears says plainly it is your next lesson
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the green star. A green bubble came up: 'Order at a café — Lesson 2 of 3 — CONTINUE +20 XP'. I did not press CONTINUE. I pressed an empty part of the path; the first press did not close it, and it closed after a second look. I finished.

screen1-a8.closing_comment: The bubble says plainly it is a lesson and which step I am on, and I value that. The star itself still has no word. I only know it is a lesson once I press it and read.

screen1-a9.where: The purple tag under the character on the left: '13 days'.
screen1-a9.expectation: Something happens in 13 days, or has gone on for 13 days. I cannot tell what, or what pressing it would do.

first_pass.why: '13 days' has no subject. It could be a countdown or a record. I would read it over and over and still not know.
first_pass.solution: Say what the 13 days are: for example '13 days left in the event'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the pill tells you what the time count refers to
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the purple pill under the owl-and-skull picture. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not tell you what the days referred to
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens says plainly what the days count
test_cases.what_happened: On my phone the purple pill said 'Ended', not '13 days'. I pressed it and the same 'Brawl Stars Quest — INCOMPLETE' page opened, with a Day 1 to Day 7 list of rewards. I closed it with the X.

screen1-a9.closing_comment: Nothing on the page explains what 'Ended' or the earlier '13 days' refers to. The page says 'INCOMPLETE' while the pill says 'Ended', which contradict each other to me. I cannot settle what the time count means.

screen1-a11.where: Path, second button down: on the running app, a round grey button with a grey star.
screen1-a11.expectation: A later lesson that I cannot open yet.
screen1-a11.cue: It is grey, like something switched off, and it sits further down the path.

first_pass.why: I infer 'locked' from the grey. Nothing says so, and nothing says which lesson it is.
first_pass.solution: A small lock and the lesson name, or a word such as 'Locked'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing a grey star says it is a lesson and that it is locked
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the first round grey star button below the green one. Read what appears. Press an empty part of the path to close it.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not say what the grey star is, or does not say it is locked
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears says plainly it is a lesson that is locked
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the first grey star below the green one. A grey bubble appeared: 'Order at a café — Complete all levels above to unlock this! — LOCKED'. Pressing an empty part of the path closed it. I finished.

screen1-a11.closing_comment: It says plainly that it is locked and what unlocks it. It does not use the word 'lesson', but 'levels' and the unit name are enough for me. A smaller difficulty than I thought.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears says plainly it is a lesson that is locked
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the first grey star below the green one. A grey bubble appeared: 'Order at a café — Complete all levels above to unlock this! — LOCKED'. Pressing an empty part of the path closed it. I finished.

screen1-a12.closing_comment: It says plainly that it is locked and what unlocks it. It does not use the word 'lesson', but 'levels' and the unit name are enough for me. A smaller difficulty than I thought.

screen1-a13.where: The grey treasure chest on the path.
screen1-a13.expectation: A reward I can open later, once I have done more lessons.
screen1-a13.cue: The picture of a chest with a lock, in grey.

first_pass.why: I can see it is a chest, but I am guessing what it gives and when I can open it.
first_pass.solution: A short caption: 'Reward: unlocks after 10 lessons'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the chest tells you what it gives and when you can open it
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the grey treasure chest on the path. Read what appears. Press an empty part of the path to close it.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not say what the chest is or when it opens
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears says plainly what the chest is and when it opens
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the grey chest. A grey bubble appeared under it saying 'Complete 10 more lessons to unlock this chest!'. Pressing an empty part of the path closed it. I finished.

screen1-a13.closing_comment: It now says plainly when it opens, which is half of what I wanted. It still does not say what is inside. So it is a smaller difficulty, not gone.

screen1-a15.where: Bottom row, fifth from left: a blue-green bird-like shape in flight.
screen1-a15.expectation: No idea. Perhaps a special mode or a paid feature.
screen1-a15.cue: Only the picture, which I cannot recognise.

first_pass.why: I cannot tell what the picture is, and there is no word. I would not dare press it.
first_pass.solution: A word under every bottom-row icon.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the bird makes plain what it is for
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the bird in the bottom row. Read what opens (do NOT press any 'try' or subscription button). Then press the house at the left of the bottom row.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not something you could have guessed from the bird
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected and you would recognise the bird next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the bird in the bottom row. A page titled 'Subscription — Compare plans' opened, showing Super, Super Family and Lite with 'TRY FOR $0.00' buttons. I did not press any of them. I pressed the house and was back on the path.

screen1-a15.closing_comment: A paid plan was only a vague guess of mine. Nothing about a bird says 'subscription', and I would not recognise it next time.

screen1-a16.where: Bottom row, first: a house, shaded blue.
screen1-a16.expectation: Takes me to the home page; I think I am on it now, because it is shaded.
screen1-a16.cue: A house is the usual picture for home, and it is highlighted.

first_pass.why: The house is a picture I know, and the shading tells me I am here.

screen1-a17.where: Bottom row, second: a yellow-orange chest-like picture.
